issues.quote: she stayed with me until after the temple struck eleven
issues.fact: R1 says Lina stayed in the kitchen until after the temple struck eleven. It does not say the temple is the hall clock, and the hall clock is a separate source in R3.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the temple and the hall clock to be the same bell and conclude Lina stayed past the hall's strike at 11:13 by the kitchen clock, which the sheet does not establish. The transcript leaves 'the temple' undefined next to 'the hall clock strike eleven', which invites that conflation.

issues.quote: The regulator on the wall had stopped.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no reading for the regulator. This detail is outside the fact sheet.
issues.misreading: A stopped regulator is a clock-related clue that invites the solver to read a time of stopping into the scene, which the sheet does not support and which could be taken as a reading attached to a different clock.

issues.quote: His little watch, the one that strikes when you press the slide, was in his hand.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no reading for this watch and does not say it struck at any time. This detail is outside the fact sheet.
issues.misreading: A repeating watch that strikes can be read as having sounded at a particular moment, which the solver could tie to the piano or the hall strikes. The sheet gives no such time.

issues.quote: When it was time for the toast, I went up the stairs to fetch the master.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no time for Rosa leaving the kitchen. It fixes only the end of Lina's stay at 'after the temple struck eleven' and the piano stopping at 11:11 by the kitchen clock.
issues.misreading: A solver could infer that Rosa stayed in the kitchen continuously from the hall strike until the toast, or that she went upstairs at a particular time. The transcript supplies no clock reading for her movements after 11:13.
